source_user: Advanced cluster case NVIDIA Dynamo-52: Design an evaluation of NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated inference orchestration. Variant 52 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate frontend routing, prefill workers, decode workers, KV movement, transport overhead, scheduling policy, queueing, model compatibility, observability, and failover behavior. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Use a read-only, version-pinned evaluation harness before changing traffic or configuration. Assume a declared model and tokenizer, context/output distributions, request mix, GPU/node/NIC topology, RDMA settings, batching, concurrency, cache warmth, software versions, tenant policy, quality threshold, and deadline; verify every version-specific claim. Hypothesis: at matched output quality and offered load, disaggregated prefill/decode orchestration lowers p95 TTFT by a predeclared amount versus co-located serving, while p99 ITL, end-to-end p99, error/timeout rate, correctness, and cost stay within predefined bounds. Compare co-located, disaggregated without KV transfer, and full disaggregation using randomized repeated trials across load, prompt-length, and warm/cold strata. Trace frontend admission/routing and queue time, scheduler placement, prefill/decode compute, KV creation/schema/version/shape/dtype/positions, serialization and transfer bytes/latency, transport retries, queue depth, GPU/network utilization, TTFT, ITL, throughput, token counts, errors, retries, and output correctness in ms, tokens/s, bytes/s, and confidence intervals. Control prompt mix, batching, model parallelism, clocking, cache state, and link contention; attribute improvements only to measured evidence. Before decode, enforce model/KV compatibility, checksum/integrity, freshness/lease, ownership fencing, authorization, and tenant isolation. Inject worker loss, RDMA degradation, stale or corrupt KV, overload, and frontend failure. Bound retries and queues, reject unsafe or unverifiable state, fall back to a known-good co-located path when available, and roll back or stop the experiment if the guardrails fail. Evidence required: version-pinned configs, topology, raw per-request traces, matched baseline results, correctness checks, fault-injection outcomes, and independent reruns; design alone proves no performance claim. Variant 52 is covered by this plan.
